entries.odia: ଏତେ ଖାଇ ନ ପୂରିଲା ପେଟ ବିରି ଓଳିଆରେ ମାରୁଛ ହାତ
entries.title: Still reaching for the pulse store
entries.literal_meaning: After eating so much, the belly is still not full; you are reaching into the stored black gram.
entries.explanation: The speaker points out a comic excess: even a substantial meal has not stopped the hand reaching for more. The dictionary places the line under having a full meal; the appetite and the reaching hand are its concrete scene. It can be read as a teasing complaint that someone has already had plenty yet still wants another share. That broader application is an editorial reading, not an additional dictionary gloss. Tone matters: the joke need not be turned into a judgment about a person’s body or genuine hunger.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏତେ ଖାଇସାରି ମଧ୍ୟ ପେଟ ପୂରିଲା ନାହିଁ, ହାତ ପୁଣି ବିରି ରଖାଥିବା ଓଳିଆ ଆଡ଼କୁ ଯାଉଛି—ଏହି ବଢ଼ିଚାଲିଥିବା ଚାହିଦାରେ କଥାଟିର ଖୋଚା। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଭୋଜନରେ ପେଟ ପୂରିବା ଅର୍ଥର ଉଦାହରଣ। ନିଜ ଭାଗରେ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ପାଇସାରି ଆହୁରି ମାଗୁଥିବା ଜଣକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଧରି ଥଟ୍ଟା କରାଯାଇପାରେ; ଏହା ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗମୂଳକ ପାଠ। ହସରେ କୁହାଯାଇଥିବା କଥା ଯେପରି କାହାର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଭୋକ କିମ୍ବା ଶରୀରକୁ ଅପମାନ ନକରେ, ସେଥିରେ କହିବାର ସ୍ୱର ଓ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିର ଫରକ ଅଛି।
entries.english_summary: A reaching hand makes a teasing picture of wanting more after already having plenty.
entries.odia_summary: ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ପାଇସାରି ମଧ୍ୟ ଆହୁରି ଚାହିଁବାକୁ ଖୋଚା ଦିଏ ଏହି ଭୋଜନର ଚିତ୍ର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: At a drawing club, everyone receives a packet of paper. One member has already taken two spare packets and now reaches for the last one. A friend laughs and quotes the saying, asking them to leave something for the others. The joke concerns their extra share, not their appetite or body.
entries.cultural_context: The food image is retained as a conversational tease. The source supplies the literal full-meal sense, not a general moral definition. The storage object is retained as ଓଳିଆ in Odia; its construction has not been independently established here.

entries.odia: ଯେବେ ପାଇଥାଏ ଘଇତାବୁକୁ, ସଜ ହେଉଥାଏ ବାପ ଘରକୁ
entries.title: An assurance, then preparations
entries.literal_meaning: When she receives encouragement or a promise from her husband, she gets ready to go to her father’s home.
entries.explanation: The local expression ଘଇତାବୁକୁ is defined as encouragement or a promise from a husband. The saying follows that assurance with the quick, visible response of getting ready to visit her parental home. The paired endings give the movement from words to preparations a light, teasing rhythm. The source does not tell us whether the promise concerns travel, money or something else, so none of those details is treated as fixed. Read as a conversational scene, it catches the eagerness with which a welcome assurance can become action.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘଇତାବୁକୁ ମାନେ ସ୍ୱାମୀଙ୍କଠାରୁ ମିଳିଥିବା ଉତ୍ସାହ ବା ଅଙ୍ଗୀକାର ବଚନ—ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ଅର୍ଥ ଦେଇଛି। ସେହି କଥା ପାଇବା ସାଙ୍ଗେ ସାଙ୍ଗେ ବାପଘରକୁ ଯିବାର ସଜବାଜ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୋଇଯାଏ। ବୁକୁ ଓ ଘରକୁର ମିଳ ଏହି ତତ୍ପରତାକୁ ହାଲୁକା ଥଟ୍ଟାର ସ୍ୱର ଦିଏ। ଅଙ୍ଗୀକାରଟି ଯାତାୟାତ, ଟଙ୍କା କିମ୍ବା ଆଉ କେଉଁ ବିଷୟରେ, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ। ମନକୁ ସୁହାଇଲା ଭଳି କଥାଟିଏ ମିଳିଲେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି କେମିତି ଚଟାପଟ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୁଏ, କଥାଟିକୁ ସେହି ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ିହୁଏ।
entries.english_summary: A welcome assurance is followed by eager preparations for a visit home.
entries.odia_summary: ମନକୁ ସୁହାଇଲା ଅଙ୍ଗୀକାର ମିଳିଲେ ବାପଘରକୁ ଯିବାର ସଜବାଜ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୋଇଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A woman has been hoping to visit her parents. Her husband offers to take over their shared errands that weekend, and she immediately starts packing. Her sister smiles and quotes the saying at the speed of the preparations. The offered help is an invented detail of this example, not part of the historical wording.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary marks the headword as a rural figurative expression. The saying presents a husband-and-wife situation; it does not establish a rule that a woman needs permission to visit her family. No particular region, marriage custom or historical incident is inferred.

entries.odia: ଜହ୍ନିଫୁଲ ପରି ଆୟୁଷ ପା ସଞ୍ଜେ ଫୁଟି ସକାଳେ ଯା
entries.title: A blessing that lasts one night
entries.literal_meaning: Have a lifespan like the jahni flower: bloom at dusk and be gone by morning.
entries.explanation: The line opens like a blessing for someone’s life, then gives that life only the span from dusk to morning. The dictionary explicitly marks it as an ironic blessing and says it is spoken in jest. That reversal, rather than a gentle wish for longevity, is the point of the joke. The flower supplies the source’s image of brevity; this explanation is not a botanical lifespan claim. Depending on the relationship and occasion, such a mock blessing can sound playful or cruel.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆୟୁଷ ପା ବୋଲି କଥାଟି ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ ଭଳି ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୁଏ, ହେଲେ ସେହି ଆୟୁଷ ସଞ୍ଜରୁ ସକାଳ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ମାତ୍ର। ଦୀର୍ଘ ଜୀବନର ଆଶାକୁ ଏମିତି ଓଲଟାଇ ଦେବାରେ ତାହାର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହାକୁ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗୋକ୍ତିମୂଳକ ଆଶୀର୍ବଚନ କହିଛି ଓ ଥଟ୍ଟାରେ କୁହାଯାଏ ବୋଲି ଲେଖିଛି। ଫୁଲ ଏଠାରେ ଅଳ୍ପ ସମୟର ଚିତ୍ର ହୋଇ ଆସିଛି। କିଏ କାହାକୁ କେଉଁ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରେ କହୁଛି, ସେହି ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ ହସ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆଣିପାରେ, ଆଘାତ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: An apparent blessing turns into a sharp joke about a life lasting only from dusk to morning.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ ଭଳି ଶୁଣାଯାଉଥିବା କଥାଟି ସଞ୍ଜରୁ ସକାଳର ଆୟୁଷ ଦେଇ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend announces yet another promise to start a daily walk tomorrow. Remembering yesterday’s abandoned plan, another friend quotes the flower blessing about the new promise, and both laugh at how briefly the last resolve lasted. Applying the image to a promise rather than a person’s life is an editorial transfer in this example.
entries.cultural_context: This is a documented mock blessing, not an instruction to wish someone harm. The printed entry’s dusk/morning wording supports the irony; no particular ceremony, speaker, first author or origin event is established. Surrounding dictionary material on a flower-related observance is a separate entry and is not imported as this saying’s origin.
entries.origin_note: Earliest use and origin unverified. Printed dictionary attestation is not proof of first composition.
